purpose: Four proposed surrounding websites; each board contains three consecutive portrait-browser frames.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE polished landscape concept board containing EXACTLY THREE large equally sized portrait mobile-browser website mockups side by side, read left to right as consecutive opening-animation keyframes of the SAME website. Plain slim gutters; no phone hardware, no perspective, no extra inset screens. Each panel is an entire fixed-height website viewport, no scrolling. Small editorial board title and frame numbers outside the viewports are okay.
This is a proposed surrounding website for the existing NEARlyHuman cozy onchain NPC game. Reference image1 establishes the approved Moss & Cream game palette and top-down Harvest Moon/GBA interior; reference2 is the actual existing phone game and today's empty surrounding background. These are style/content references, NOT edit targets. Design the website AROUND that game. Preserve the existing square pixel-art game composition, sharp navy beveled HUD, status icons, little rooster, warm wooden kitchen and concise navy dialogue box. The final third viewport must display the large playable square game at nearly full available phone width, surrounded by an attractive finished website. The outer artwork must still be present around it after the reveal; never return to an empty cream background. Do not redesign the game, stretch it into a portrait game, reduce it to a tiny thumbnail, put illustrations over its controls, or turn this into a marketing page.
Visual direction: nostalgic original Saturday-morning cartoon, charming 2D illustration, confident balanced art direction. Restrained warm cream, moss green, midnight navy, honey yellow and small terracotta accents; lively contrast rather than washed-out gray. Thoughtful uncluttered negative space with character. Full-height mobile-first layout. The three frames are opening → transformation → actual game in its finished surrounding website. Imagine a brief skippable reveal built from a few lightweight layers; no progress bars, artificial waiting, menus to unlock the game or long copy. Only brand text “NEARlyHuman” where appropriate, tiny skip during intro, tiny sound control if appropriate. Avoid web3 branding clutter, gradients, photorealism, glossy3D and unrelated new game mechanics.
CONCEPT A — SATURDAY MORNING PREMIERE. Character-led hand-painted cel cartoon with expressive navy ink, clean flat painted shapes and slight print warmth. Frame1: a small cream-and-gold cartoon rooster pokes through a circular opening in an inviting graphic stage, curious and playful, surrounded by rounded concentric cream/moss/honey shapes. Frame2: a beautifully composed “NEARlyHuman” cartoon title card with the same rooster peeking around its lettering, the circular opening growing into a rounded-square aperture. Frame3: that aperture has expanded into the existing crisp square pixel game, visually dominant, with a small wordmark above; the illustrated rings now form a gently receding full-viewport background and the rooster peeks from the outer lower edge without blocking anything. The final site feels like the cartoon episode has become playable. Distinct hand-drawn character charm; do not make it a TV appliance or a house exterior. Board title “01 · SATURDAY MORNING”. Make all three stages feel like one continuous composition.

CONCEPT B — THE COZY TELEVISION. An original beautifully illustrated retro CRT set, warm friendly Saturday morning ritual, flat 2D cel drawing with navy outlines and cream/moss/honey casing, little rabbit-ear antenna and one appealing oversized dial. Frame1: the illustrated television is the protagonist, screen asleep with a tiny warm line of light, within an artfully minimal domestic backdrop. Frame2: the screen blooms into a small rooster-shaped channel ident and “NEARlyHuman”; the casing naturally expands toward the viewport edges as the picture opens. Frame3: the existing square pixel game fills a LARGE undistorted screen almost the full phone width; the slim casing remains around it as the website's permanent character. Move the dial/controls below the screen, not beside it, so they never steal game width. Casing only at the outer edges; no glass glare, curved game image, thick black surround or unreadable small game. A small plant and warm flat wall shapes may provide quiet peripheral charm; the game is the star. Board title “02 · THE COZY CRT”. Preserve consistent framing across the three stages.

CONCEPT C — COME ON IN. A lovingly drawn cartoon version of the NPC's little house, original 2D animation-background art, a few bold painted shapes and dark navy ink, cream plaster, honey roof, moss garden, warm light, a cloud drifting. Not isometric, not a realistic architectural render. Frame1: a charming small house exterior under a welcoming morning sky, one square window glowing invitingly, a little rooster silhouette inside, tasteful NEARlyHuman title integrated overhead. Frame2: a smooth visual push toward the SAME square window, shutters opening, the pixel kitchen just beginning to be visible inside; roof and leaves slide toward the edges. Frame3: the window has become a large clean rectangular frame around the existing sharp square pixel game, taking nearly the entire phone width; a little eave, shutters kept far outside the game, vine and garden shapes at the viewport margins maintain the illustrated setting. The decorative exterior must never imply the game itself has become hand-drawn. The finished website surrounds a real game as if looking into the NPC's home. Board title “03 · COME ON IN”. Cohesive camera movement; rich but restrained, no clutter and no fictional game controls.

CONCEPT D — YOUR OWN CARTOON CHANNEL. A crisp flat retro broadcast station ident, bold geometric shapes, delightful graphic-design composition, old cartoon network energy without copying any existing brand. This is distinct from hand-drawn concentric cartoon rings and from a physical TV set: use expressive blocky lettering, offset rectangles, shooting four-point stars, checkerboard/slanted stripe accents and a small rooster emblem. Frame1: a confident navy full-height graphic canvas with cream/honey/moss shapes sweeping across it, small NEARlyHuman wordmark, a playful star marking the motion. Frame2: the same shapes part in a dynamic rectangular wipe, a large delightful NEARlyHuman station title briefly aligns while the warm pixel house begins to emerge in the central square. Frame3: an airy balanced finished broadcast-style website with the existing large square pixel game sharp and prominent, small station-style wordmark above, an asymmetric arrangement of a few restrained flat shapes continuing around the margins, quiet cream/honey/navy areas above and below. Do not use static noise, color test bars, fake channel selection, progress text or technical diagnostics. The third screen should feel welcoming and settled, with enough decorative identity to fix the blank-background problem. Board title “04 · CARTOON CHANNEL”. One coherent graphic movement leads to the game.
